key_insight: Understanding AI requires mapping not just its technical layers, but also the organizations connecting them. This project frames the AI supply chain as a network of dependencies that can help reveal vulnerabilities and market concentration.
problem_solved: The relationships among organizations supplying AI models, data, compute, capital, and talent are sparsely documented, making ecosystem-wide dependencies difficult to assess.
method: Focus on organizations involved in AI development and deployment rather than technical components alone.
Examine cross-layer relationships among providers of models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets.
Use a supply-chain perspective to frame dependency, vulnerability, and concentration questions; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify detailed methods or results.
impact: An organizational supply-chain view can help AI/ML practitioners assess reliance on external providers and consider resilience when choosing partners and infrastructure. Specific findings cannot be verified from the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Layered ecosystem diagram showing models, data, compute, capital, and talent connected through organizations.
Organization network map with node size representing connectivity and edges representing dependencies.
Dependency-path diagram illustrating how disruption at one provider could affect downstream AI development or deployment.
Illustrative concentration chart showing how a few providers could serve many downstream organizations, clearly labeled as conceptual.
paper_title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
paper_authors: Sarah H. Cen, Lindsey A. Gailmard, Joohan Kim, Rishi Bommasani, Daniel E. Ho
